From the owner
Kitchen Lighting Guide: Best Design Tips for Custom Kitchens Essential Kitchen Lighting Ideas for Your New Custom Kitchen Most homeowners spend weeks choosing custom cabinets and countertops, then make their lighting decisions in an afternoon. That's a mistake. We will show you why you should always overthink your kitchen lighting. Must-know kitchen lighting design tips for your new kitchen start with one core principle: lighting does more work in a kitchen than in almost any other room. It supports prep, cooking, cleaning, and entertaining — often all at once. Get it wrong and even a beautifully designed luxury kitchen feels dim, flat, or frustrating to use. Why Kitchen Lighting Deserves More Thought Than Most Decisions Kitchen lighting affects how you see food, how safe the workspace feels, and how the room looks morning through evening. A single overhead fixture — the default in many new builds — creates shadows on countertops and leaves the edges of the room in gloom. Cooking in those conditions isn't just inconvenient. It can be a safety issue. Lighting also affects how the kitchen feels. A bright, evenly lit space reads as clean and functional. A kitchen with layered, dimmable light sources reads as warm and considered. The difference is rarely about budget — it's about planning. Decisions made early, before walls are closed and cabinets installed, give you far more options and lower installation costs. Click below to read more:
